Record date: 2130-01-21
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 01/21/30 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Persistent shortness of breath, worsening cough, and ongoing fatigue despite treatment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up after two days of inpatient management for COPD exacerbation and pneumonia. The patient reports minimal improvement in his respiratory symptoms since the initiation of intravenous Piperacillin/Tazobactam. He continues to experience significant dyspnea, particularly with exertion and at rest, and describes his cough as increasingly productive with a persistent foul odor. Mr. Fairfax notes that he has experienced a slight decrease in his fever but continues to have night sweats that disrupt his sleep.
The patient expresses frustration with his lack of progress and reports continued fatigue, which he attributes to both his respiratory condition and the side effects of Prednisone. He has not noticed any significant change in his appetite or weight.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, + intermittent fevers, + night sweats, - weight loss. Pulmonary - + worsening productive cough with foul-smelling greenish sputum, + wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain, - orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - + decreased appetite, - nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - no joint pain. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 130/76 mmHg - Heart Rate: 92 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 28 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 85% on supplemental oxygen (8 L via nasal cannula).
General: The patient appears fatigued and is in moderate respiratory distress, using accessory muscles for breathing.
HEENT: No nasal flaring; oropharynx clear, no signs of dehydration.
Lungs: Marked wheezing on auscultation; decreased breath sounds bilaterally; prolonged expiration with rhonchi; crackles audible throughout lung fields.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops; peripheral pulses intact.
Extremities: No edema; no tenderness on palpation.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation with persistent bacterial pneumonia, evidenced by ongoing respiratory symptoms, hypoxemia, and limited response to initial antibiotic therapy. 2. Continued hypoxemia necessitating adjustment of oxygen therapy and further evaluation of respiratory function. 3. Significant fatigue likely exacerbated by systemic steroid therapy and underlying respiratory pathology.
PLAN
1. Transition intravenous Piperacillin/Tazobactam to oral Amoxicillin/Clavulanate 875 mg every 12 hours, as sputum culture results indicate sensitivity to this agent; continue monitoring for clinical response. 2. Continue oral Prednisone at 80 mg daily with a planned taper depending on clinical improvement; consider adding a proton pump inhibitor for gastric protection given the prolonged steroid use. 3. Maintain supplemental oxygen at 8 L via nasal cannula and reassess oxygen saturation; consider a trial of BiPAP if the patients respiratory status does not improve. 4. Repeat chest X-ray to evaluate for any new complications, including potential effusion or worsening pneumonia. 5. Continue nebulized bronchodilator therapy (Albuterol) every four hours as needed; increase frequency if wheezing persists; consider adding Ipratropium bromide for enhanced bronchodilation. 6. Schedule a follow-up visit within 48 hours or sooner if symptoms worsen; discuss the potential for pulmonary rehabilitation once stabilized.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax continues to be closely monitored in the internal medicine unit. The treatment team will adjust the management plan based on his clinical progress, with particular attention to his respiratory function and overall stability. The patient is encouraged to communicate any new or worsening symptoms promptly, and education regarding the importance of adherence to the modified antibiotic regimen and ongoing therapy will be reiterated.
